transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I suppose the main reason is that something’s been happening at school, and I know it may sound a bit strange when I say it out loud. I teach secondary school, and lately I can’t shake this feeling that some of the staff emails and even the morning announcements are… not just ordinary announcements. They feel like they’re worded in a way that’s about me, or meant for me, like there’s another message underneath the usual one.

For example, an email will go out to everyone about “professional conduct” or “being mindful of tone,” and I’ll read it and feel certain it’s referring to something I said or did, even if my name isn’t there. And with the morning announcements, it can be a phrase or the timing of it, and I find myself thinking, “That’s aimed at me.” My colleagues have been kind about it, really—they’ll show me that the email was sent to the whole staff, or say it’s just a routine notice—but even then the feeling doesn’t fully go away. I can understand what they’re saying, but I still keep wondering if there’s something coded in it.

It’s been upsetting because I don’t want to be difficult at work, and I don’t want to misread people, but I keep getting pulled back into it. That’s why I came in.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Yes… yes, I have. Not constantly, and it isn’t like a crowd of people or anything dramatic like that, but there have been times when I’m quite sure I’ve heard someone when no one was there.

It’s usually a woman’s voice. Sometimes when I’m at home and the house is quiet, I’ll hear my name said very clearly, almost as if someone is in the next room trying to get my attention. And a few times after the classroom has emptied, when I’m tidying up or putting books away, I’ve heard a short comment about what I’m doing. Nothing long, just a brief remark, but clear enough that I’ve actually answered out loud before catching myself and realizing there’s nobody there.

That’s the part that unsettles me, because it doesn’t feel like just a thought in my head at the time. It feels like I’ve heard it with my ears, if that makes sense. Then I look around, and of course there’s no one there, and I feel embarrassed even though no one’s seen it.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, excited, or full of energy for days at a time?

I’m not sure I’d describe anything as “unusually high,” no. I mean, I do have days where I’m a bit more wound up or busy, especially if there’s a lot happening at school, but I don’t think I’ve had days and days where I’m excited or full of energy in a way that felt out of character.

If anything, when things are stressful I can get preoccupied and restless, but that feels more like tension than being on top of the world or anything like that. I don’t think I’ve noticed the sort of thing you’re asking about.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think so, no—not most of the day nearly every day. I do get upset and worn down by everything that’s been happening, and there are evenings when I come home feeling quite low or discouraged, like I’ve been carrying too much around all day. But I wouldn’t say it’s this steady depression from morning to night, every day.

It’s more that I feel strained, if that makes sense. Sometimes sad, sometimes anxious, sometimes just tired and fed up with myself for not being able to let things go. But I still have periods where I’m functioning, doing my lessons, getting through ordinary things. So… no, I haven’t noticed being depressed in that constant way you’re describing.
How long have these experiences been going on?

I’d say about four months, roughly. It’s a little hard to pin it down exactly, because at first I kept explaining it away as being tired or stressed, or thinking I’d misheard something.

But the worries about things having some sort of coded meaning, and the woman’s voice that I sometimes actually answer before realizing no one is there… those have been going on for around four months now. Not every minute of every day, but enough and for long enough that I can’t really dismiss it anymore.
Over the past four months, has your ability to do your job or manage daily life gotten noticeably worse?

Yes… I think it has, though I’ve been trying very hard not to let it show. I’m still teaching, so from the outside it might look as if I’m managing, and in some ways I am. I still get into school, I still stand in front of the class, I still mark work and do the ordinary routine as best I can.

But it’s not quite the same as before. I’ve needed other teachers to step in more than I would like, especially during project lessons where there are lots of moving parts and noise and questions coming from everywhere. I used to be quite good at keeping all of that organized, but lately I find myself losing the thread or needing someone else to take over a section or help settle things.

Planning meetings have been harder too. I can get through them, but sometimes only because a colleague quietly helps me keep track or nudges things along. I don’t like admitting that, because I’ve always prided myself on being competent and prepared.

And outside work, yes, I’ve dropped off a lot. I used to be reliable for book club, going to the theater with friends, neighborhood events—that sort of thing. Now I cancel, or I say I’ll help and then don’t follow through properly, or I just avoid committing because I’m worried I won’t manage it. So yes, it’s noticeable. Not a complete collapse, but definitely worse than I was.
